==English==
{{was wotd|2022|February|6}}

===Etymology===
[[File:Treatyofwaitangi.jpg|thumb|The “Waitangi sheet”, one of [[nine]] [[document#Noun|documents]] which [[make up]] the {{w|Treaty of Waitangi}} ''(sense 2.2)'', [[regard#Verb|regarded]] as the [[founding#Adjective|founding]] document of [[New Zealand]]. This sheet was the first to be [[sign#Verb|signed]] by the [[consul]] for the [[British#Adjective|British]] [[Crown]] and [[Māori]] [[chief#Noun|chiefs]] at [[Waitangi]] on 6 February 1840.]]

The {{glossary|noun}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|trete}}, {{m|enm|trety|t=bargaining, negotiation; discussion; conference, meeting; entreaty, persuasion; agreement, contract, covenant; arrangement, settlement; agreement between two rulers, states, etc.; written work on a particular subject, treatise; subdivision of a written work, section}}{{nb...|(Late Middle English) trate, (Middle English) traite, traitee, traitie, traitye, traytee, traytte, trayttye, traytye, treatye, treetee, tretee, tretei, treti, tretie, tretty, tretye|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=trētẹ̄|pos=''n.''(3)|noformat=1|id=MED46986}}</ref> from {{der|en|xno|treté}}, {{m|xno|traité}}, {{m|xno|treaté}}, and {{der|en|fro|traité}}, {{m|fro|traitié}}{{nb...|traieté, traitei|otherforms=1}} (modern {{cog|fr|traité|t=agreement between two rulers, states, etc.; treatise}}); {{m|fro||traité}} or {{m|fro||traitié}} is:<ref name="OED">{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=205395|date=December 2021|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref>

* a noun use of the {{glossary|past}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|fro|traiter|t=to treat; to deal with, handle}}, from {{der|en|la|tractāre}}, the {{glossary|present}} {{glossary|active}} {{glossary|infinitive}} of {{m|la|tractō|t=to drag, haul, tug; to handle, manage; to debate, discuss; to exercise, practise; to perform, transact}}, from {{m|la|trahō|t=to drag, pull}} + {{m|la|-tō|pos={{glossary|frequentative}} {{glossary|suffix}}}}; and
* also from {{der|en|la|tractātum|t=written work on a particular subject, treatise}}, from {{der|en|la|tractātus|t=dragged, hauled, tugged; handled, managed; exercised, practised; performed, transacted}}, the {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|tractō}} (see above).

The {{glossary|verb}} is derived from the noun.<ref name="OED"/>

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|countable|international law}} A [[formal]] [[binding#Adjective|binding]] [[agreement]] [[conclude]]d by [[subject#Noun|subjects]] of [[international law]], namely, [[state#Noun|states]] and [[international#Adjective|international]] [[organizations]]; a [[convention]], a [[pact#Noun|pact]].
#: {{usex|en|to sign a peace '''treaty'''}}
#: {{usex|en|to write up a '''treaty''' touching climate change}}
#* {{RQ:Bacon Henry 7|page=47|passage=[T]he ''Duke of Britaine'' hauing beene an ''Hoſte'', and a kind of ''Parent'' or ''Foſter-father'' to the King, in his tenderneſſe of age, and vveakneſſe of fortune, did looke for at this time from King {{smallcaps|Henry}} (the renovvned King of ''England'') rather braue ''Troupes'' for his Succours, then a vaine '''''Treatie''''' of Peace.}}
#* {{RQ:Burnet History|volume=I|page=15|passage=Soon after his [{{w|James VI and I}}'s] coming to the Crown of ''England'' he entered into ſecret '''treaties''' with ''Spain'', in order to the forcing the States to a peace: {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Adam Smith Wealth of Nations|volume=II|chapter=Of the Principle of the Commercial, or Mercantile System|page=29|passage=Exportation was encouraged ſometimes by dravvbacks, ſometimes by bounties, ſometimes by advantageous '''treaties''' of commerce with foreign ſtates, and ſometimes by eſtabliſhment of colonies in diſtant countries.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}}
## {{lb|en|uncountable}} ''Chiefly in'' '''in treaty''': [[discussion]]s or [[negotiation]]s in order to [[reach#Verb|reach]] an [[agreement]].
##* {{RQ:Evelyn Diary|volume=I|entrydate=30 April 1680|page=519|passage=To a meeting of the executors of late Visc{{sup|sse}} Mordaunt's estate, to consider of the sale of Parsons Greene; being in '''treaty''' with Mr. Loftus, and to settle the halfe yeare's account.}}
## {{lb|en|countable}} ''Chiefly in'' '''[[private#Adjective|private]] treaty''': an agreement or [[settlement]] reached following negotiations; a [[compact#Noun|compact]], a [[contract#Noun|contract]], a [[covenant#Noun|covenant]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}}
## {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[manner#Noun|manner]] or [[process#Noun|process]] of [[treat#Verb|treating]] someone or something; [[treatment]]; also, the manner in which someone or something [[act#Verb|acts]] or [[behave]]s; [[behaviour]].
##* {{RQ:Jonson New Inne|scene=iii|page=35|passage=''Hoſ''[''t'']. They call me Good-ſtock. / ''Lov''[''el'']. Sir, and you confeſſe it, / Both i'your language, '''treaty''', and your bearing.}}
## {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[address#Verb|addressing]] or [[consideration]] of a [[subject#Noun|subject]]; discussion, treatment.
## {{lb|en|countable}} A [[formal#Adjective|formal]], [[systematic#Adjective|systematic]] [[discourse#Noun|discourse]] on some subject; a [[treatise]].
##* {{RQ:Browne Pseudodoxia Epidemica|edition=2nd|chapter=Of the Second Cause of Popular Errors; the Erroneous Disposition of the People|page=7|passage=And though {{w|Galen}} doth ſometime nibble at [[w:Moses|Moſes]], and beſide the Apoſtate Chriſtian, ſome Heathens have queſtioned his Philoſophicall part or '''treaty''' of the Creation: Yet is there ſurely no reaſonable Pagan, that will not admire the rationall and well grounded precepts of Chriſt; {{...}}}}
##* {{RQ:Burnet History|volume=I|page=326|passage=The Miniſters in ''Holland'' did upon this occaſion ſhew a very particular violence. In their ſermons, and in ſome printed '''treaties''', they charged the Judges with corruption, who had carried the ſentence no farther than to baniſhment: And compared the fate of the ''De Wits'' to ''{{w|Haman}}''’s.}}
## {{lb|en|countable}} An [[act#Noun|act]] of [[beseeching#Noun|beseeching]] or [[entreating#Noun|entreating]]; an [[entreaty]], a [[plea#Noun|plea]], a [[request#Noun|request]].
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Antony and Cleopatra|act=III|scene=xi|page=356|column=1|passage=Now I must / To the young man ſend humble '''Treaties''', dodge / And palter in the ſhifts of lovvnes, vvho / VVith halfe the bulke o' th' vvorld plaid as I pleas'd, / Making, and marring Fortunes.}}
